title: Compatibility probe service, pin expiry policy, and routing shim for graceful runtime-version fallbacks
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Background: As runtime and model versions proliferate, we need a robust, automated way to route traffic to compatible model/runtime pairings while allowing fast rollouts. Current pinning is manual and brittle: pins persist indefinitely, compatibility checks are ad-hoc, and when a runtime upgrade introduces behavioral changes some customers see silent failures or degraded latency.

Goals:
- Provide a lightweight compatibility probing service that tests candidate runtime/model pairings before routing live traffic.
- Introduce a pin-expiry policy and automated soft-fallback so stale pins do not block upgrades indefinitely.
- Implement a routing shim that can perform per-request compatibility checks (fast path) and fall back to last-known-good pairing when probes fail.
- Provide observability: probe success rates, probe latency, pin age, and rollback triggers surfaced in Console dashboards.

Proposal summary:
1) Compatibility probe service (compat-prober): runs short synthetic requests against a model-runtime pairing, validates schema, tokenization sanity, and response latency. Probes run at two cadences: pre-route (blocking canary rollout) and ongoing background (safety probes).
2) Pin expiry policy: pins have TTL metadata (default 30 days). When TTL expires, routing moves to an automatic compatibility window where compat-prober runs targeted probes before deciding whether to renew the pin or evict it.
3) Routing shim: a lightweight in-proxy component evaluates per-route routing policy. If a request arrives for a pinned model and the pinned runtime is unhealthy, the shim attempts a fast compatibility probe (cached results for <30s) and if that fails, routes to a configured fallback variant (e.g., quantized model or previous runtime LTS).
4) Rollout gates: new runtime versions are gated by a preflight probe pass, traffic-percent canary, and a regression-detection policy based on correctness metrics (eval set pass-rate) and latency.

Non-goals: full semantic regression detection for generative quality (this ties into Optimize/evals work) and any changes to billing model.

Trade-offs considered:
- Probe fidelity vs speed: we choose short, targeted probes that check critical compatibility invariants rather than full-quality evals to keep rollout fast.
- Autos-renewing pins vs explicit renew: default is auto-renew after successful probes with audit log record; orgs can opt-out to manual renewals.
decisions:
1) Implement compat-prober as a service in control plane (k8s) with sidecar-compatible HTTP probe endpoints.
2) Default pin TTL = 30 days, configurable per-tenant.
3) Routing shim caches probe results for 30s and uses soft-fallback to previous LTS runtime when probe fails more than 3 times in a 1-minute sliding window.
4) Canary gating requires both probe success and no regression in the canary eval suite; if regressions are detected routing automatically scales back to the last stable channel and alerts SRE/PM.
acceptance_criteria: compat-prober deployed to staging and runs scheduled probes against runtime-1.20 candidates
routing shim returns fallback within 50ms after probe failure and does not add more than 10ms p50 to healthy requests
pin TTL applied and renew path exercised in a staging tenant (renew true and renew false flows)
Console dashboard shows probe success rate, pin age distribution, and a simulated canary rollback event
e2e test: upgrade path from runtime-1.19 -> runtime-1.20 produces zero customer-facing 5xx errors in synthetic traffic and falls back automatically in induced failure scenario
